summary: Hideaki Nakatani is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University in 1966 under Gadjin Nagao, was a disciple of Yutaka Ochihara, earned a PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and was a professor at Kobe Gakuin University (attested 2003).
Hidehiko Kurita works in religious studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Tohoku University and served as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University (attested 2020).

Hidehiro Okada (1931–2017) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1957) and under Nicholas Poppe at the University of Washington (~1957–1959), later serving at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1966–1993) and Tokiwa University (~1996–2002).
Hideki Kiyoshima (born 1951) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Delhi. He served as a lecturer at Kindai University (attested 1989).
Hidemasa Nagata (1933–2024) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1953 to 1961 and later held a post there from ~1963 to 1996.

Hidenaka Tanaka (1886–1974) studied at the University of Tokyo (1906–1912) under Raphael von Koeber, the University of Oxford (1922–1924), and Kyoto University (doctorate, 1930). Working in linguistics, he held posts at the University of Tokyo, Kyoto University, and Kyoto Women's University.

Hidenori Kitagawa (1920–1978) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Hakuju Ui. He was a Rockefeller Foundation fellow (1952–1953) and served as a professor at Nagoya University (attested 1968–1969).

Hidenori S. Sakuma (born 1954) studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. A Buddhist, Indology, and Tibetology scholar, he held posts at Shitennoji University, Otani University, Taisho University, and University of Tsukuba.

Hideo Mineshima (1927–2013), a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied at Taisho University and Waseda University. He held academic posts at Waseda University (1960–1998), Sanko Research Institute, and Bunkyo Gakuin University, and headed several scholarly and religious organizations.

Hideomi Yaita (born 1953) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University. He held posts as a research assistant at Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1991–1995) and lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995).
Hidetaka Fukazawa (born 1956) is a religious studies scholar who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1975–1979). He held a post at Hitotsubashi University around 1990.
Hidetaka Nakatani is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University in 1966 under Gadjin Nagao.
Hideto Ono (born 1944) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University (~1963–1967). He served as an associate professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).

Hidetoshi Yoshizawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts at Taisho University as a researcher (attested 1998), lecturer (attested 2008), and chief research fellow (attested 2017), as well as at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute (attested 2006).

Hidetsugu Yagi (1886–1976) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909). During his career, he held posts at Tohoku University (~1919–1932), the University of Tokyo (~1934–1942), Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1942–1944), and Osaka University (~1946–1947).

Hideyo Ogawa (born 1954) is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He held posts at Hiroshima University as an associate professor (~1989–1996) and later as a professor (~1996–2020; attested 2026).

Hideyuki Matsumori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Soka University (attested 2006) and later held positions there as assistant professor (attested 2015) and professor (attested 2026).

Hilko Wiardo Schomerus (1879–1945), a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied under Nathan Söderblom and Paul Deussen at Kiel and Leipzig. He held academic positions at Kiel University (1918–1923) and was an ordinary professor at Halle-Wittenberg from 1926.

Himanshu Prabha Ray (born 1947) studied at Panjab University, Cambridge, and Jawaharlal Nehru University. Specializing in Indology and archaeology, she was an associate professor at JNU (1980–2012) and held appointments at the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies, Munich, and National Monuments Authority.

Hinrich Middeldorpf (1788–1861) was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1806–1810). He held a post at the University of Breslau from ~1813 to 1861.
